title: Regime-Dependent Growth Enhancement: A Transition Metric Interpretation of the Fugaku–DESI Matter Density Offset
description: The paper reinterprets the ~10% matter-density offset seen in DESI-calibrated Fugaku N-body simulations as an integrated transition-strength estimator, ΔF ≈ 0.1, of a regime-dependent effective gravitational coupling μ(a) ≡ G_eff/G. It introduces a bounded transition kernel and an observational window W(a) to define ΔF, and shows a single μ(a) can satisfy CMB (μ≈1 at recombination), DESI/Fugaku growth (ΔF≈0.1 in the sensitivity band), and galaxy-scale (μ→1+Δμ) consistency simultaneously.

effective_gravitational_coupling.description: Dimensionless, time-dependent effective gravitational coupling encoding growth modifications without altering the homogeneous background.

transition_kernel.description: Smooth, bounded transition in log-scale factor; R(x) is a monotonic regulator with R(-\infty)=0 and R(+\infty)=1, centered at a_t with width \sigma and amplitude \Delta\mu.

transition_estimator.description: Integrated transition strength over the DESI/Fugaku observational sensitivity window W(a); empirically calibrated to \Delta F \approx 0.1.

key_results.main_finding: The DESI-calibrated Fugaku matter-density offset is best interpreted as an integrated transition metric with \Delta F \approx 0.1, realizable by a single \mu(a) that respects CMB, large-scale structure, and galaxy-scale constraints.

sealed_predictions.statement: Independent implementations of the transition estimator in Boltzmann and structure-growth solvers, when fit to DESI DR2 BAO/RSD together with Fugaku-like N-body outputs, will recover a positive integrated transition strength consistent with \Delta F \approx 0.1 within the DESI sensitivity window.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint CMB+BAO/RSD+simulation-informed growth analyses that robustly favor \Delta F consistent with zero or negative values over the DESI/Fugaku window.

kill_criteria: KC1: Independent re-analyses of Fugaku-class N-body outputs calibrated to DESI DR2, using at least two distinct Boltzmann/structure solvers implementing the estimator, fail to recover a positive integrated transition strength and instead prefer Delta_F consistent with zero across the DESI window.

KC2: High-precision CMB analyses allowing time-dependent \mu(a) detect a statistically significant deviation from a recombination-era plateau (i.e., \mu(a \ll a_t) \neq 1), violating the required CMB consistency condition.

KC3: A comprehensive, regime-aware meta-analysis of galaxy rotation curves demonstrates that late-time asymptotic enhancement (\mu \to 1+\Delta\mu > 1) is disfavored, or requires \mu \leq 1, contradicting the galaxy-scale consistency condition.

KC4: The ~10% matter-density proxy observed in DESI-calibrated Fugaku-class simulations is shown to be a numerical or pipeline artifact (e.g., eliminated by higher resolution, alternative force solvers, or improved systematics control), removing the empirical basis for mapping the offset to \Delta F \approx 0.1.

KC5: Cross-redshift and multi-probe fits demonstrate that no smooth, bounded regulator R(x) with any (a_t, \sigma, \Delta\mu) can simultaneously satisfy the three consistency conditions (CMB plateau, \Delta F in the DESI window, and late-time \mu>1), invalidating the single-transition-kernel hypothesis.

KC6: Joint BAO+RSD+weak-lensing growth measurements robustly indicate growth suppression in the DESI sensitivity band (i.e., significantly negative \Delta F), contradicting the regime-dependent growth enhancement claim.
abstract_short: Reinterprets ~10% matter density offset in Fugaku N-body simulations as transition estimator Delta_F approx 0.1 measuring integrated regime transition strength rather than fundamental density parameter.
